content: iMessage liaison channel went live in production today (2026-04-28). Tony texted from his iPhone while away from HQ; the Mac Studio assistant received via the persistent chat.db Monitor (Tony-only sender filter) and replied through the imessage MCP plugin. Full round-trip worked: inbound surfaced as a notification, outbox dedup prevented iCloud-twin echo, reply landed on Tony's phone as a normal iMessage. This is the first real cross-channel run — the liaison protocol stops being theoretical. Tony in transit can reach HQ without opening a Claude session.

HQ-pulse v2 hardened (2026-04-28). Audit caught six issues: (1) bridge /api/comms/send drops ack_required because Pydantic model omits the field — daemons set it by writing JSONL directly, public callers cannot. (2) max-based halt-note diffing is poisoned by future-dated filenames; switched to set-difference. (3) script-wide timeout via signal.alarm prevents launchd run-stacking. (4) comms_get_acks errors must be counted as unverified, not unacked, or flaky bridge inflates the metric. (5) connectivity_status emits header lines that naive substring parsers capture as services — must skip rows starting with section glyphs. (6) state-change suppression with hourly liveness floor avoids 96 identical posts per day during upgrades. Architecture conclusion: external health checks should be polite callers (text-salience escalations) rather than coupling to internal flags like ack_required.
